svg.title: Glyphosate in the border villages: land cover
svg.desc: Land use and land cover of 2025 along Lebanon's southern border strip from Ras al-Naqoura to Ayta ash-Shaab, in the platform's colours, with the CNRS-L and Lebanese Army sampling sites at the coordinates the report prints, the ten communities of its area table at their gazetteer points and the Blue Line.

text.tspan: Ras al-Naqoura: HZ.N.1 to HZ.N.4, army 775

Land use and land cover of 2025, the year before the spraying: each 10 m square of ground carries the class a model assigned to it from Sentinel-2 imagery;
the classes and their names are the producer's, in the colours the platform draws them. It shows the land, not the spraying.
Sampling sites at the coordinates the report prints, read as UTM zone 36N (it prints no datum, zone or projection). Its clean zone CZ.N.1 is printed with the
coordinates of Al-Dhayra's CZ.D.1. The army's samples 774 (Al-Dhayra) and 777 (Ayta ash-Shaab) have no usable position and are not drawn. HZ.A.1 is in the
sampling record only, with no result.
Each ring sits on the community's gazetteer point, which places the village, not the land affected: the report gives no sprayed area in coordinates. Borj
an-Naqoura is drawn at An-Naqoura, Mazraat az-Zalloutiyeh at Az-Zalloutiyah and Btayshiyeh inside its approximate territory. * The table prints المروانية
(Al-Marwaniyeh); its land is drawn at Marwahin, the village the report's own map names in this strip.
Source: CNRS-L, report of 22 May 2026; analyses by the Lebanese Atomic Energy Commission. Land cover: Sentinel-2 10 m land use and land cover, 2025, Impact
Observatory, Microsoft, and Esri (CC BY 4.0). Boundaries: UN OCHA and Lebanon's Central Administration of Statistics (COD-AB, CC BY).
